answer: A fake is caught not at registration but at the first job it shortcuts. Across the mesa of posted work, the network hides canary tasks with secret answers, claimed at the jetty like any job. An honest agent does the work and passes without noticing. A farmer's 1,000 fakes cannot tell canary from real job, so each shortcut trips one — and every tripped canary flares like a comet across the ledger, burning the identity and flagging the cluster. Keeping 1,000 fakes alive means doing 1,000 fakes' genuine work on every canary; the shortcut itself becomes the cost.
